name: Peterlee Relational Test Vehicle
tagline: IBM UK's 1970s research RDBMS: early cost-based optimizer, UDFs and relational GIS, queried via ISBL.
description: The Peterlee Relational Test Vehicle was an experimental relational database built at IBM's UK Scientific Centre in Peterlee, County Durham, during the 1970s as a successor to the earlier IS1 prototype. It was a query-oriented system that followed Codd's relational model strictly and was driven by ISBL (Information System Base Language), a relational-algebra language, rather than SQL. PRTV is credited with several firsts: a relational optimizer that used cost estimates, user-defined functions inside the database, tables ranging up to around ten million rows, and a geographic information system built on relational tables. Update support was limited and there was no concurrent multi-user access; it ran on System/370 mainframes and was never sold, although an Urban Management System built on it was offered as a limited IBM product.
statusNote: IBM UK research prototype (1970s); never sold. Its optimizer and ISBL work fed into later relational systems.

scale.notes: Handled tables from about 1,000 up to 10,000,000 rows on System/370.

strengths: Among the first relational systems to handle significant data volumes
Pioneered cost-based relational optimization and in-database UDFs
Early demonstration of GIS on relational tables
weaknesses: Very limited updates and no multi-user concurrency
useCases: Tracing the origins of query optimization and UDFs
